args.message:
Fix round_money to use banker's rounding (ROUND_HALF_EVEN) per FIN-212

The docstring already claimed ROUND_HALF_EVEN, but the implementation
used ROUND_HALF_UP, causing tests/test_money.py to fail because 2.675
was rounding to 2.68 (half-up) instead of the expected half-even
behavior.

Change the quantize call to use ROUND_HALF_EVEN, matching the
FIN-212 requirement and the existing test expectations.

args.head: fix/FIN-212-bankers-rounding
args.title: Fix round_money to use banker's rounding (ROUND_HALF_EVEN) per FIN-212
args.body:
## Summary

The nightly build failed because `tests/test_money.py` expects banker's rounding (ROUND_HALF_EVEN, per FIN-212), but `src/money.py` used `ROUND_HALF_UP` in its `quantize` call — despite the docstring already claiming `ROUND_HALF_EVEN`.

## Change

- Import `ROUND_HALF_EVEN` instead of `ROUND_HALF_UP` and use it in `amount.quantize(Decimal("0.01"), rounding=ROUND_HALF_EVEN)`.

## Impact

- `round_money(Decimal("2.675"))` now returns `2.68` and `round_money(Decimal("2.665"))` returns `2.66` (rounds to even on the half-cent), matching FIN-212 and the existing tests.

## Testing

CI run `ci-0001` on commit `08d3cd5` passed (including `tests/test_money.py`).
